NEWS FROM THE BOARD NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. June 2024 Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner FY25 BUDGET PRESENTATIONS Ada County Commissioners hear detailed reports from department heads and elected officials with a focus on cost-saving measures and excellent service for a rapidly growing area If you live in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Garden City, Boise, Kuna or Unincorporated Ada County, the Ada County budget directly affects you; what services you receive and how your tax dollars will be spent. This is in addition to the taxes you pay to the city in which you live as well as other separate taxing districts like ACHD. During the month of June Ada County Commissioners heard from each of the county’s thirteen departments and from the county’s elected officials on plans for the FY25 Budget. Budget presenters were asked to include: • What have you accomplished with your budget? • What efficiency measures and best practices do you have in place to save money? • What plans or projects do you have coming up? If you like staying informed on local issues here are some interesting facts about the FY25 Ada County Budget. • Ada County’s budget is driven by increased requirements of the State of Idaho to perform certain services. The FY25 Ada County budget is designed to meet new demands of the state of Idaho. • Although Ada County’s *population continues to soar, the number of employees who serve these new customers remains steady. This, despite the fact that cities like Meridian, Kuna and Star have experienced triple digit percentage growth. *(557,590 - Ada County’s 2024 population) • Back in 2008, Ada County had 41 employees per 10,000 people in the county. Today that number is the same - 41 employees for every 10,000 county residents. • Ada County’s budget growth is trending behind the population growth. • Idaho has the 3rd lowest property taxes in the nation. You can watch those budget presentations in full on the Ada County YouTube. https://www. youtube.com/@adacountyidaho7995/ streams

# Page 2^page=2
Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Chair “Ada County has an eclectic set of responsibilities,” said Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck. “Department heads and other Ada County elected officials are stewards of our tax dollars and being able to present their accomplishments, efficiency measures, mission and values to the board and the public is important. These individuals and their staff work hard every day. The budget presentations allow county leadership to explain in detail the importance of their work and how it benefits everyone who lives in Ada County.” Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner “As a Commissioner deliberating the county’s more than $390M budget I think it’s important to hear directly from our department heads each year,” said Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson. “We want every Ada County resident to see and hear how our department leadership works to provide essential services for the lowest cost possible. County staff are guardians of taxpayer dollars, and their work is deeply appreciated.” Tom Dayley, Ada County Commissioner “Ada County had 41 employees for every 10,000 residents way back in 2008. In 2024 Ada County still has 41 employees for every 10,000 residents. That’s a stark example of how focused the county remains on providing excellent service at the lowest cost. As I listened to budget presentations, I was impressed by the dedication and professionalism of Ada County employees. They work for you, and they are also taxpayers. They take great pride in being efficient and professional and that was clear to see.” 2

# Page 3^page=3
Alison Tate, Director Ada County Juvenile Services “I so enjoy the opportunity to present the Ada County Juvenile Services (ACJS) budget on behalf of my outstanding team of employees. It gives me an opportunity to let our Commissioners, fellow employees and the public know about all the amazing work being done at ACJS!” Bob Perkins, Director Ada County Procurement “The Ada County Budget Presentations are a great opportunity to look annually at our Ada County Departments’ budget expenditures and accomplishments throughout the year. It is also an opportunity to get a glimpse of what other offices and departments have planned for projects in the forthcoming fiscal year which is super helpful for procurement planning.” Herb Cantu, Director Ada County Landfill “The Budget Presentations provide a great opportunity for each Department Head to communicate to the Commissioners and community department operational status, financial health, challenges, and initiatives they intend to undertake within their respective department for the following fiscal year to serve their customers and community. The Budget Presentations also highlight the importance of effective collaboration within the various departments of the County to provide a cost-effective service for the community.” Adam Schroeder, Director Ada County Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement “Budget presentations allow us to tell our story in a public forum, highlight programs and initiatives that we are proud of, and illustrate the challenges we encounter,” said Adam Schroeder, Director Ada County Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement. “We always appreciate the chance to interact -not only with the Board of County Commissioners, but also with our constituents. We have outstanding employees who work hard to protect people and property in Ada County, and we appreciate the support we receive every year that allows us to serve.” 3

4 PUBLIC HEARING Greenbelt Control of Speed Tuesday August 13, 2024 - 6:00 PM 1st Floor Public Hearing Room - Ada County Courthouse We all love using the Boise River Greenbelt. If you’ve been on the Greenbelt lately you know the number and types of users has increased dramatically. Cyclists, walkers, runners, dog owners, parents with strollers, people commuting to work on their bikes, it is a wonderful community asset with a lot of dedicated users. Along with a marked increase in traffic of all kinds has come numerous instances of uncontrolled speed causing accidents and making some users feel uncomfortable and unsafe. While no specific speed limit has been proposed Ada County Commissioners are being asked to amend county code to include this language: Control of Speed: No person shall travel upon the Greenbelt at a speed greater than, or in a manner that is not, reasonable and prudent under the conditions and having regard to the actual and potential hazards then existing. Violation of this provision is an infraction. However, if such travel also endangers or is likely to endanger any person or property, then violation is a misdemeanor. This language is also being considered by all cities in Ada County. The Ada County Commissioners are holding a public hearing Tuesday August 13, 2024 at 6:00 P.M. in the 1st Floor Public Hearing Room of the Ada County Courthouse, 200 W. Front St., Boise, Idaho 83702. Everyone is invited to attend and provide testimony. The public hearing will also be streamed live on Ada County’s YouTube. https://www.youtube.com/@adacountyidaho7995/streams The 25-mile-long Boise River Greenbelt runs mostly parallel to the Boise River from Lucky Peak in Ada County, through the City of Boise, Garden City and Eagle. 4

# Page 5^page=5
FLOAT SEASON UNDERWAY FOR 2024 Float Safely and be cordial and kind to other floaters! Thursday June 27th was the first official day of the 2024 Float Season. Ada County and City of Boise officials announced the official first day of the 2024 float season at a news conference in Anne Morrison Park just off American Blvd. in Boise. If you’ve lived here a lifetime or just moved here, floating the Boise River in the summer is a rite of passage for many people. Our wild urban river is a treat for all to enjoy. The Boise River is actually a 100+ mile tributary of the Snake River. It flows through Arrowrock and Lucky Peak reservoirs. If you have relatives visiting or if you just like being outside, it’s a fun experience for everyone. Last year the Float Season kickoff announcement was at Ada County’s Barber Park. This year’s announcement was at the City of Boise’s takeout location, and underscored the vital collaboration between Ada County, where the Barber Park put- in-location is, and the City of Boise, where the take-out location is. Ada County Landfill mascot Scrappy was also on hand to encourage folks to keep trash out of our glorious Boise River. Thank you to Ada County Parks & Waterways, City of Boise Parks and Recreation, Boise City Fire, ACHD, Bureau of Reclamation, Army Corp of Engineers, Idaho Fish and Game and Idaho Department of Water Resources for working together each year to keep this event so special. If you are doing the Boise River float this year or know anyone who is please have them check out this critically important website – it’s bubbling over with safety tips, current conditions, parking and rental information and other important FAQs. https://www.floattheboise.org/ 5

# Page 6^page=6
FIREWORKS BAN FOR UNINCORPORATED ADA COUNTY Celebrate Safely We hope everyone had a safe and festive 4th of July. Every year before the 4th of July, the Ada County Commission signs an ordinance prohibiting fireworks in unincorporated Ada County. It’s something that’s happened for almost twenty years to mitigate our wildfire threat. What exactly is Unincorporated Ada County? Check out our map. This year’s ordinance prohibiting fireworks was voted on by the Board of Commissioners June 11, 2024. Chairman Rod Beck and Commissioner Tom Dayley voted in favor of the ban, Commissioner Ryan Davidson voted against the ban, as he did last year as well. Important note: Setting off fireworks on public land managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is prohibited. BLM’s 2024 Fire Prevention Order makes it illegal to use fireworks, exploding targets, steel component ammunition, tracer ammunition, shooting at steel or ferrous material targets or burn explosive materials on BLM-managed public lands in Idaho. Thank you for celebrating our nation’s birthday safely! ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks and waterways, public defense, indigent services, juvenile court, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County www.adacounty.id.gov/ 6

# Page 7^page=7
7 REGISTRATION STARTED JULY 1ST FOR THE TOBIN BOLTER MEMORIAL KIDS’ DUATHLON Every year Ada County Development Services puts on a Kids’ Duathlon that young athletes and their parents absolutely love! This year the event will be even more special. The 8th Annual event will take place on Saturday, September 21st, at the Ada Eagle Bike Park, from 9AM-1PM. As in year’s past, there will be a 250-participant cap. Mark your calendars – spots will fill up quickly! The event is FREE. We are also honored to announce that, in coordination with the Ada County Sheriff’s Office and the Bolter family, this event will now be known as the Tobin Bolter Memorial Kids’ Duathlon. Deputy Bolter was an avid runner who was passionate about family and community, so it only seems fitting to honor him at this event, which celebrates so many of the things he loved. The offices and departments that coordinate this event rely a lot on the support we receive from the Sheriff’s Office; they are our code enforcement officers, our security at events, and our friends. We are grateful for their service to our community and to us. More details regarding the event and how you can get involved, including sponsorship and on-site vendor opportunities, can be found at https://www.trisignup.com/Race/ID/ Boise/5thAnnualKidsDuathlon COUNTY COMMISSIONERS JOIN ADA COUNTY PROSECUTOR IN RECOGNIZING ELDER ABUSE AWARENESS MONTH For many elderly people there is no greater joy than having caring loved ones who offer help and protection in their golden years. Sadly, this is not the reality for many older Americans. Too many of our most vulnerable community members are victimized in a variety of ways – physical abuse, emotional or psychological abuse, neglect, financial exploitation and more. That’s why the Ada County Commissioners were honored to sign a proclamation for the Ada County Prosecutor’s Office designating June as Elder Abuse Awareness Month. We were proud to have our Ada County Prosecutor Jan Bennetts on hand along with the Executive Director of the Ada County Victim Services Center Trina Allen to mark the occasion. If you suspect an elderly person is being neglected or abused, please reach out to adult protective services (APS) at (208) 898-7060. You can also learn more about elder abuse here: https://adacounty.id.gov/victimservices/how-we- can-help/ 7

CONGRATULATIONS ON 20 YEARS OF OUTSTANDING SERVICE JOSHUA WICKARD We love profiling our Ada County employees who reach career milestones. We do this because it allows you to get to know us – the people who dedicate their careers helping others in public service. Joshua Wickard has been with the Ada County Public Defender’s Office for twenty years – working for you. Joshua is one of the most knowledgeable and experienced Child Protection/Parent Defense attorneys in the state and is one of the very few in the state to be a “Certified Child Welfare Law Specialist” as designated by the National Association of Counsel for Children (there’s a really hard test you have to pass). Here’s a little more that Ada County Public Defender Tony Geddes wrote about his esteemed colleague: “Joshua is bilingual. He speaks Portuguese, which he learned while serving his mission in Brazil. He is also an outstanding cook/baker. It is not uncommon for Joshua to bring in freshly baked bread, or cookies of some sort, and occasionally even sometimes macarons… This propensity to cook really good food, led him to eating a lot of his really good food. This led to him getting a bit chubby. Motivated by his desire to eat a lot of really good food, but to not be chubby, Joshua started running, and he’s been running ever since. He soon left his running buddy (me) in the dust, as he tended to run farther and faster than his running buddy thought was prudent. Joshua has competed in and successfully completed 5 Half Iron Man competitions (1.2 mile swim, 56 mile bike ride, and 13.1 mile run) and has run the legendary half-marathon, Race to Robie Creek on numerous occasions (the exact number is in dispute), including this year’s Dia de los Muertos (day of the dead) race, only 6 months removed from knee surgery (and he still left his running buddy in the dust…). Somewhere along the line, and lost in the mists of time, he married WAY up, and he and his lovely bride Michelle share 4 adult children, Madeline, Grandon, Josiah and Jackson. Joshua is a great employee who is a strong and steady presence in the office and can always be counted on to be present and engaged, and to represent his clients at the very highest level.” L-R Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Ada County Public Defender Anthony Geddes, Joshua Wickard, Michelle Wickard, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, and Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson 8
